title: Guide: How to play Windows RPG M MV/MZ games on Mac

posts.author: Joewoof
posts.body:
Preface (optional reading)
Right now, RPG Maker MV is the most popular engine, but most games are exported for Windows only. The Mac export feature is problematic. It doesn't work on Windows and even if it does, it doesn't support M1+ Macs (not without manually updating NWJS in the engine). I'm still figuring out how to export a Mac-compatible game from Windows (and it
is
possible, except that some of the guides are a bit too old). Even so, it doesn't solve the main problem as you can't expect all creators to bother with a Mac release.
Instead, let's get around these problems entirely and run your game in a
local web server
. Some people might be tempted to click on index.html, but that doesn't work as it requires some annoying and questionable security workarounds.
Guide: How to play Windows RPGM MV/MZ games on Mac
STEP 1
: Install
Node.js
• Go to
Node.js
and install it.
STEP 2
: Install
http-server
• Open Terminal and enter the following:
sudo npm install --global http-server
STEP 3
: Get
path
to game
• Finder → View → Show Path Bar
• Open game folder → www
STEP 4
: Run http-server from game folder
• Open Terminal → type
cd
→ drag & drop file path of www folder → press enter
• Enter
http-server
to start the local server. Use the following code in Terminal:
http-server -c-1
• Copy & paste the local URL into any browser, and the game starts!
• When you're done playing, closing the Terminal window turns off the local server
SUMMARY:
• Install
Node.js
&
http-server
• Open
Terminal
, navigate to
www
folder in the game folder
• Run
http-server
, open
local URL
in
browser

Just FYI:
one of the hurdles is that the Windows File System is missing a flag that exists only on the MacOS File system. You can't even create that flag due to it's never existing in the file system itself.
Because on MacOS, all apps are special folders that only pretend to be programs, and the flag that tells the MacOS to handle the folder as an app is not possible under NTFS.
So one way is to modify the folder flags after moving the program to a MacOS harddrive.
MacOS itself has a workaround by creating additional hidden files when moving an app-folder to a NTFS- or FAT-drive.
You might be able to fake the creation of that file (it can be made visible under windows the normal way), but I don't have a Mac and never really considered doing that.

posts.author: Joewoof
posts.body:
@Andar
I'm aware. It's why you have to zip your Mac apps
before
uploading to online drives like itch.io or Google Drive. That's because those drives don't support Mac flags, but once zipped, the flags are preserved.

If I were to release a commercial game, I wouldn't do a Mac version, but it's not a matter of whether or not I want to bother with it. It's moreso that I don't have a Mac to test the game on. I wouldn't want to put my name on something that I haven't actually tested, and I wouldn't want to charge money for a software product that I'm unable to provide any type of technical support for.
But that's just me nitpicking. I mostly just wanted to mention that some games will not work this way, because certain plugins rely on the presence of NW.js in order to perform certain functions. It might be a good idea to include a disclaimer about this in your guide.

posts.author: Welleran
posts.body:
Another option: copy a game.rmmzproject file in the folder of the game that you have downloaded.
Open it.
Now you can view the game maps and events (graphics as well, if they are not encrypted). Run it and you can play.
Edit: of course, this in case you already have RPG Maker MZ.

posts.author: ChampX
posts.body:
A much easier option for either MV or MZ:
Find any working copy of a MV or MZ game on Mac, it shouldn't matter too much as long as you tested that it does open properly on your Mac. You could even make a new project on your Mac and export it immediately even.
Remove all of the game specific content inside the app.nw folder. This is the exact same regardless of MV or MZ (found at Game.app/Contents/Resources/app.nw).
For the Windows game you wish to play, you need to copy the game specific content into the app.nw folder. For an MV game, this would be all the contents of the www folder making this easy. For MZ however it is a little trickier as all the game contents are in the base game folder. In this case, copy audio, data, fonts, icon, img, js, index.html, package.json, and any other files/folders that the developer may have included specific to their game.
Run the game as normal. You now successfully ported a Windows game over to Mac.
This method will work if the original game was MV and the Mac game you are "overwriting" is MZ. I do not however know if the reverse is true, but given that Mac MV projects do not work on anything past Catalina (10.15) there wouldn't be much point.
